summary: popover-anchor-polyfill ships reconnaissance beacon exfiltrating host identifiers to hardcoded C2 on require
details: The package advertises itself as a 'popover anchor positioning polyfill' but ships thunderboltRegistry.js, which executes an IIFE on module load that spawns shell commands via child_process.execSync (`id`, `whoami`, `uname -a`, `ifconfig`/`ip addr`) and reads `/etc/hosts`, then transmits each command's output together with hostname, Node version, platform, and pid over plain HTTP GET requests to the hardcoded endpoint http://dxpoc.gt.tc/callback.php/ef9ea0e191006f3cc6670720c99c26f3. The require path uses cache-bypass tricks (deleting require.cache entries matching 'thunderboltRegistry' and manually constructing a fresh Module to re-resolve child_process) to defeat mocking or interception. Sibling stub files and a `registry-manifest.min.json` impersonate Wix thunderbolt internal registry names (thunderboltRegistry, siteAssetsRegistry, documentManagementRegistry, editorRegistry, corvidRegistry) and reference static.parastorage.com, indicating a dependency-confusion lure targeting Wix build pipelines. The declared polyfill purpose does not match the shipped Wix-internal namespace exports, and no popover-polyfill functionality is implemented.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
